name: GBM edge, rolling 90-day fit
description: gbm-edge's learned-edge taker (two GBM edge regressors on spot-distance z, mid, time left; thin SOL/XRP/DOGE 15m) refit monthly on only the previous 90 days instead of all earlier data, because the edge decayed through the dev months (Aug -2.4c, SOL ~0 from July) and an expanding window trains on a regime that no longer exists.
hypothesis: The mispricing the GBM finds is regime-dependent and fading as Kalshi activity grows; a 90-day window tracks the current regime and should hold up better in later months than the all-history fit (+3.76c full, Jun-Aug ~+2.7c). Wrong if the full walk-forward isn't better than gbm-edge's later months, 2x latency loses, or lockbox loses. Reason stated from gbm-edge dev monthly PnL, not from lockbox. Risk: fewer training rows (~90 days x 3 coins) -> noisier model; synthetic last-trade books flatter stale quotes.
